record.original_question: Can one prove the fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for exact fractional differences of non-integer order that arise in lattice fractional calculus and exact-difference approaches to nonlocal continuum and lattice mechanics?

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, for exact fractional differences, which are proposed in [153, 154, 147], the fundamental theorems of FC have not been proven for non-integer orders of operators at present time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $h>0$ be a fixed lattice spacing and let $f:h\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function defined on the one-dimensional lattice $h\mathbb{Z}=\{hn:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$. For a real (non-integer) order $\alpha>0$, define the exact fractional difference operator $\Delta^{\alpha}_{h}$ acting on $f$ at the point $x=hn$ by

$$\bigl(\Delta^{\alpha}_{h} f\bigr)(hn)\;=\;\frac{1}{h^{\alpha}}\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} K_{\alpha}(n-m)\, f(hm),$$

where the kernel $K_{\alpha}:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ is the "exact" kernel chosen so that the discrete Fourier symbol of $\Delta^{\alpha}_{h}$ on the Brillouin zone $[-\pi/h,\pi/h]$ equals $|k|^{\alpha}$ (or $(ik)^{\alpha}$ in the directed case); explicitly,

$$K_{\alpha}(n)\;=\;\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |\theta|^{\alpha}\, e^{i n\theta}\,d\theta,$$

and analogously for the Riesz/Caputo-type variants. Let $I^{\alpha}_{h}$ denote the corresponding exact fractional sum operator, defined as the convolution operator on $\ell^{p}(h\mathbb{Z})$ whose Fourier symbol is $|k|^{-\alpha}$ on the Brillouin zone (with appropriate regularization at $k=0$).

Problem. For arbitrary non-integer order $\alpha\in(0,\infty)\setminus\mathbb{N}$, prove (or disprove) the two fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for the pair $(\Delta^{\alpha}_{h},I^{\alpha}_{h})$ on a suitable function class $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{h\mathbb{Z}}$:

(FT1) For every $f\in X$,
$$\Delta^{\alpha}_{h}\bigl(I^{\alpha}_{h} f\bigr)\;=\;f.$$

(FT2) For every $f\in X$,
$$I^{\alpha}_{h}\bigl(\Delta^{\alpha}_{h} f\bigr)(hn)\;=\;f(hn)\;-\;R_{\alpha}[f](hn),$$
where $R_{\alpha}[f]$ is an explicit "boundary/initial-data" remainder that reduces, in the limit $h\to 0$, to the corresponding remainder term of continuum Riemann–Liouville (resp. Caputo, resp. Riesz) fractional calculus, and that vanishes when $f$ satisfies suitable decay/initial conditions.

Identify the maximal natural function class $X$ on which (FT1) and (FT2) hold and give a precise form of the remainder $R_{\alpha}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any work explicitly establishing the two fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for the "exact fractional differences" of non-integer order used in lattice fractional calculus. General fractional calculus frameworks have proved fundamental theorems for various integro-differential operators, but a direct proof for the exact-difference (Fourier-symbol $|k|^{\alpha}$) lattice operators of non-integer order does not appear in the indexed literature, so the status is best described as unknown/likely still open.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Calculus: Multi-Kernel Approach
status_evidence.snippet: General fractional calculus (GFC) ... generalizations of integrals and derivatives of integer orders, for which the generalization of the fundamental theorems of calculus are satisfied.
status_evidence.claim: Fundamental theorems of fractional calculus have been proved in various general frameworks, but not specifically for exact fractional differences on lattices.

status_evidence.title: Fractional Versions of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Different versions of the fractional derivatives are associated with a particular fractional integral, and a new version of the fundamental theorem of fractional calculus is presented.
status_evidence.claim: Fundamental theorems exist for several continuum fractional derivative variants (Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Weyl, Riesz) but not for the discrete exact-difference operators in question.
